+func runExportCheckpoint(w, _ io.Writer, checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
+	content *checkpoint.SessionContent, summary *checkpoint.CheckpointSummary,
+	showcase bool, format, outputFile string) error {
+
+	// Prepare transcript for export
+	transcriptBytes := content.Transcript
+	prompts := content.Prompts
+	contextMd := string(content.Context)
+	filesTouched := content.Metadata.FilesTouched
+
+	// Apply redaction if showcase mode
+	if showcase {
+		cfg, err := settings.Load()
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("loading settings: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		showcaseConfig := cfg.GetShowcaseConfig()
+		if showcaseConfig == nil {
+			showcaseConfig = &redact.ShowcaseConfig{}
+			*showcaseConfig = redact.DefaultShowcaseConfig()
+		}
+
+		// Layer 1: Existing entropy-based redaction
+		transcriptBytes, err = redact.JSONLBytes(transcriptBytes)
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("entropy redaction failed: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		// Layer 2: Showcase redaction (patterns, blocklist, structural)
+		transcriptBytes, err = redact.ShowcaseJSONL(transcriptBytes, *showcaseConfig)
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("showcase redaction failed: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		prompts = redact.Showcase(prompts, *showcaseConfig)
+		contextMd = redact.Showcase(contextMd, *showcaseConfig)
+
+		filesTouched = make([]string, len(content.Metadata.FilesTouched))
+		for i, path := range content.Metadata.FilesTouched {
+			filesTouched[i] = redact.Showcase(path, *showcaseConfig)
+		}
+	}
+
+	// Format output
+	var output []byte
+	var err error
+
+	switch format {
+	case "json":
+		output, err = formatExportJSON(checkpointID, content, summary,
+			transcriptBytes, prompts, contextMd, filesTouched)
+	case "markdown":
+		output, err = formatExportMarkdown(checkpointID, content, summary,
+			transcriptBytes, prompts, contextMd, filesTouched)
+	default:
+		return fmt.Errorf("unsupported format: %s", format)
+	}
+
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("formatting failed: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// Write output

+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write output: %w", err)
+		}

+		}

+package cli
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
+)
+
+// formatExportJSON formats checkpoint data as JSON.
+func formatExportJSON(checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
+	content *checkpoint.SessionContent, summary *checkpoint.CheckpointSummary,
+	transcript []byte, prompts, context string, filesTouched []string) ([]byte, error) {
+
+	out := map[string]any{
+		"checkpoint_id": checkpointID.String(),
+		"session_id":    content.Metadata.SessionID,
+		"metadata": map[string]any{
+			"created_at":  content.Metadata.CreatedAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
+			"strategy":    content.Metadata.Strategy,
+			"agent":       content.Metadata.Agent,
+			"token_usage": content.Metadata.TokenUsage,
+		},
+		"transcript":    string(transcript), // JSONL as string
+		"prompts":       prompts,
+		"context":       context,
+		"files_touched": filesTouched,
+		"exported_at":   time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339),
+	}
+
+	// Include summary if available
+	if content.Metadata.Summary != nil {
+		out["summary"] = map[string]any{
+			"intent":     content.Metadata.Summary.Intent,
+			"outcome":    content.Metadata.Summary.Outcome,
+			"learnings":  content.Metadata.Summary.Learnings,
+			"friction":   content.Metadata.Summary.Friction,
+			"open_items": content.Metadata.Summary.OpenItems,
+		}
+	}
+
+	return json.MarshalIndent(out, "", "  ")
+}
+
+// formatExportMarkdown formats checkpoint data as Markdown.
+func formatExportMarkdown(checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
+	content *checkpoint.SessionContent, summary *checkpoint.CheckpointSummary,
+	transcript []byte, prompts, context string, filesTouched []string) ([]byte, error) {
+
+	var sb strings.Builder
+
+	// Header
+	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "# Session: %s\n\n", content.Metadata.SessionID)
+	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "**Checkpoint:** `%s`\n\n", checkpointID.String())
+	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "**Created:** %s\n\n", content.Metadata.CreatedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))
+
+	// Summary section (if available)
+	if content.Metadata.Summary != nil {
+		sb.WriteString("## Summary\n\n")
+		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "**Intent:** %s\n\n", content.Metadata.Summary.Intent)
+		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "**Outcome:** %s\n\n", content.Metadata.Summary.Outcome)
+
+		if len(content.Metadata.Summary.Learnings.Code) > 0 {
+			sb.WriteString("**Key Learnings:**\n\n")
+			for _, l := range content.Metadata.Summary.Learnings.Code {
+				fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "- %s: %s\n", l.Path, l.Finding)
+			}
+			sb.WriteString("\n")
+		}
+	}
+
+	// Files section
+	if len(filesTouched) > 0 {
+		sb.WriteString("## Files Modified\n\n")
+		for _, file := range filesTouched {
+			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "- `%s`\n", file)
+		}
+		sb.WriteString("\n")
+	}
+
+	// Transcript section - reuse existing formatting
+	sb.WriteString("## Transcript\n\n")
+	formattedTranscript := formatTranscriptBytes(transcript, "")
+	sb.WriteString(formattedTranscript)
+
+	return []byte(sb.String()), nil
+}

+func TestExport_Showcase_EndToEnd(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	RunForAllStrategies(t, func(t *testing.T, env *TestEnv, strategyName string) {
+		// Setup repository and branch
+		env.InitRepo()
+		env.WriteFile("README.md", "# Test")
+		env.GitAdd("README.md")
+		env.GitCommit("Initial commit")
+
+		if strategyName == "manual-commit" {
+			// Switch to feature branch for manual-commit strategy
+			env.GitCheckoutNewBranch("feature/test")
+		}
+
+		// 1. Create a session with a checkpoint
+		session := env.NewSession()
+		if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(session.ID); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
+		}
+
+		// 2. Make code changes with sensitive data
+		apiCode := `package api
+
+import "github.com/lib/pq"
+
+// Connect to 10.0.1.5:5432
+const dbConn = "postgres://user:pass@10.0.1.5:5432/db"
+
+func Handler() {
+	// Admin email: admin@acme-corp.com
+}
+`
+		env.WriteFile("src/api.go", apiCode)
+
+		configCode := `package config
+
+const Key = "sk-proj-test-secret-key"
+const InternalURL = "https://api.internal.company.com"
+`
+		env.WriteFile("src/config.go", configCode)
+
+		// 3. Create checkpoint
+		session.CreateTranscript(
+			"implement API handler with database connection",
+			[]FileChange{
+				{Path: "src/api.go", Content: apiCode},
+				{Path: "src/config.go", Content: configCode},
+			},
+		)
+		if err := env.SimulateStop(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
+		}
+
+		// 4. Commit to make it a committed checkpoint
+		env.GitAdd("src/api.go", "src/config.go")
+		env.GitCommit("feat: add API handler")
+
+		// 5. Extract checkpoint ID from commit
+		headHash := env.GetHeadHash()
+		checkpointID := env.GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(headHash)
+		if checkpointID == "" {
+			t.Fatal("no checkpoint ID in commit message")
+		}
+
+		// 6. Export with showcase mode (JSON format)
+		output, err := env.RunCLIWithError("explain", "-c", checkpointID, "--export", "--showcase", "--format=json")
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("export failed: %v, output: %s", err, output)
+		}
+
+		// 7. Verify JSON structure
+		var exported map[string]any
+		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(output), &exported); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("invalid JSON output: %v\nOutput: %s", err, output)
+		}
+
+		// Check required fields
+		requiredFields := []string{"checkpoint_id", "session_id", "transcript", "metadata", "files_touched", "exported_at"}
+		for _, field := range requiredFields {
+			if _, ok := exported[field]; !ok {
+				t.Errorf("missing required field: %s", field)
+			}
+		}
+
+		// 8. Verify redaction - sensitive data should be redacted
+		transcriptStr, ok := exported["transcript"].(string)
+		if !ok {
+			t.Fatal("transcript not a string")
+		}
+
+		// Sensitive data that should be redacted
+		sensitivePatterns := []string{
+			"sk-proj-test-secret-key", // API key (entropy-based)
+			"10.0.1.5",                  // Private IP (pattern-based)
+			"postgres://",               // DB connection string (pattern-based)
+			"admin@acme-corp.com",       // Email (pattern-based)
+			"api.internal.company.com",  // Internal URL (pattern-based)
+		}
+
+		for _, pattern := range sensitivePatterns {
+			if strings.Contains(transcriptStr, pattern) {
+				t.Errorf("sensitive data not redacted: %q found in transcript", pattern)
+			}
+		}
+
+		// Should contain redaction markers
+		if !strings.Contains(transcriptStr, "REDACTED") && !strings.Contains(transcriptStr, "[") {
+			t.Error("no redaction markers found in transcript")
+		}
+
+		// Transcript should still be valid JSONL
+		lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(transcriptStr), "\n")
+		for i, line := range lines {
+			if len(line) == 0 {
+				continue
+			}
+			var entry map[string]any
+			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &entry); err != nil {
+				t.Errorf("line %d not valid JSON: %v\nLine: %s", i, err, line)
+			}
+		}
+	})
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,281 @@
+package redact
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"regexp"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// ShowcaseConfig controls showcase-specific redaction for public sharing.
+// This applies additional privacy-focused redaction beyond standard entropy detection.
+type ShowcaseConfig struct {
+	RedactPaths       bool     // Normalize file paths (e.g., /Users/x/project/src → src/)
+	RedactUsernames   bool     // Replace usernames/emails
+	RedactProjectInfo bool     // Replace repo/project names from git remotes
+	AllowedPaths      []string // Paths to preserve (e.g., "src/", "lib/")
+	AllowedDomains    []string // Domains to keep (e.g., "@example.com")
+	CustomBlocklist   []string // Additional terms to redact (glob patterns)
+}
+
+// DefaultShowcaseConfig returns sensible defaults for showcase redaction.
+func DefaultShowcaseConfig() ShowcaseConfig {
+	return ShowcaseConfig{
+		RedactPaths:       true,
+		RedactUsernames:   true,
+		RedactProjectInfo: true,
+		AllowedPaths:      []string{"src/", "lib/", "cmd/", "pkg/", "internal/"},
+		AllowedDomains:    []string{},
+		CustomBlocklist:   []string{},
+	}
+}
+
+// Showcase applies showcase redaction after standard entropy-based redaction.
+// Call String() or JSONLBytes() first, then apply Showcase() for layered protection.
+func Showcase(s string, cfg ShowcaseConfig) string {
+	result := s
+
+	// Layer 1: Pattern-based redaction
+	result = redactPatterns(result)
+
+	// Layer 2: Blocklist matching
+	result = redactBlocklist(result, cfg.CustomBlocklist)
+
+	// Layer 3: Structural normalization
+	if cfg.RedactPaths {
+		result = redactFilePaths(result, cfg.AllowedPaths)
+	}
+	if cfg.RedactUsernames {
+		result = redactUsernames(result, cfg.AllowedDomains)
+	}
+	if cfg.RedactProjectInfo {
+		result = redactProjectInfo(result)
+	}
+
+	return result
+}
+
+// ShowcaseJSONL applies showcase redaction to JSONL session data.
+// Preserves JSON structure while redacting values.
+func ShowcaseJSONL(b []byte, cfg ShowcaseConfig) ([]byte, error) {
+	var buf bytes.Buffer
+	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(bytes.NewReader(b))
+
+	// Increase buffer size for large lines (up to 10MB per line)
+	maxCapacity := 10 * 1024 * 1024
+	scanBuf := make([]byte, maxCapacity)
+	scanner.Buffer(scanBuf, maxCapacity)
+
+	for scanner.Scan() {
+		line := scanner.Bytes()
+		if len(line) == 0 {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		// Parse JSON to preserve structure
+		var entry map[string]any
+		if err := json.Unmarshal(line, &entry); err != nil {
+			// Fallback: treat as plain string
+			redacted := Showcase(string(line), cfg)
+			buf.WriteString(redacted)
+			buf.WriteByte('\n')
+			continue
+		}
+
+		// Recursively redact values (but not keys)
+		redactJSONValues(entry, cfg)
+
+		// Re-serialize
+		redactedLine, err := json.Marshal(entry)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal redacted JSON: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		buf.Write(redactedLine)
+		buf.WriteByte('\n')
+	}
+
+	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to scan JSONL: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	return buf.Bytes(), nil
+}
+
+// redactJSONValues recursively redacts values in JSON objects/arrays while preserving keys.
+func redactJSONValues(v any, cfg ShowcaseConfig) {
+	switch val := v.(type) {
+	case map[string]any:
+		for key, child := range val {
+			switch childVal := child.(type) {
+			case string:
+				// Redact string values (but not keys)
+				val[key] = Showcase(childVal, cfg)
+			case map[string]any, []any:
+				// Recurse into nested structures
+				redactJSONValues(childVal, cfg)
+			}
+		}
+	case []any:
+		for i, child := range val {
+			switch childVal := child.(type) {
+			case string:
+				val[i] = Showcase(childVal, cfg)
+			case map[string]any, []any:
+				redactJSONValues(childVal, cfg)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// Pattern-based redaction
+
+var (
+	// Internal URLs and private IPs
+	internalURLPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\b[a-z0-9-]+\.(internal|local|corp|lan)\b(:[0-9]+)?`)
+	privateIPPattern   = regexp.MustCompile(`\b(?:10\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}|172\.(?:1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}|192\.168\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3})(?::[0-9]+)?\b`)
+
+	// Cloud ARNs
+	awsARNPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`arn:aws:[a-z0-9-]+:[a-z0-9-]*:[0-9]{12}:[a-zA-Z0-9/._-]+`)
+	gcpPattern    = regexp.MustCompile(`projects/[a-z0-9-]+/[a-zA-Z0-9/._-]+`)
+
+	// Database connection strings
+	dbConnPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)(postgres|postgresql|mongodb|mysql|redis)://[^\s\)\"\']+`)
+
+	// Email addresses (basic pattern)
+	emailPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b`)
+
+	// AWS account IDs (12 digits in AWS context)
+	awsAccountPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)(aws|account|arn)[\s:][^\s]*?([0-9]{12})\b`)
+
+	// JWT tokens (starts with eyJ)
+	jwtPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\b`)
+
+	// PEM private keys
+	pemKeyPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`-----BEGIN[A-Z ]+PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]*?-----END[A-Z ]+PRIVATE KEY-----`)
+
+	// File paths with user directories
+	homePathPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`/(?:Users|home)/[^/\s]+`)
+)
+
+func redactPatterns(s string) string {
+	result := s
+
+	result = internalURLPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[INTERNAL_URL]")
+	result = privateIPPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[PRIVATE_IP]")
+	result = awsARNPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[AWS_ARN]")
+	result = gcpPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[GCP_RESOURCE]")
+	result = dbConnPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[DB_CONNECTION_STRING]")
+	result = emailPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[EMAIL]")
+	result = jwtPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[JWT_TOKEN]")
+	result = pemKeyPattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[PEM_PRIVATE_KEY]")
+
+	// AWS account IDs - preserve context, redact number
+	result = awsAccountPattern.ReplaceAllStringFunc(result, func(match string) string {
+		return awsAccountPattern.ReplaceAllString(match, "${1} [AWS_ACCOUNT_ID]")
+	})
+
+	return result
+}
+
+func redactBlocklist(s string, blocklist []string) string {
+	result := s
+
+	for _, pattern := range blocklist {
+		// Convert glob pattern to regex
+		regexPattern := globToRegex(pattern)
+		re := regexp.MustCompile("(?i)" + regexPattern)
+		result = re.ReplaceAllString(result, "[REDACTED]")
+	}
+
+	return result
+}
+
+func redactFilePaths(s string, allowedPaths []string) string {
+	result := s
+
+	// Redact absolute paths with user directories
+	result = homePathPattern.ReplaceAllStringFunc(result, func(match string) string {
+		// Check if path starts with any allowed prefix
+		for _, allowed := range allowedPaths {
+			if strings.Contains(match, "/"+allowed) {
+				// Extract relative path from allowed prefix
+				parts := strings.Split(match, "/"+allowed)
+				if len(parts) > 1 {
+					return allowed + parts[len(parts)-1]
+				}
+			}
+		}
+		return "[PATH]"
+	})
+
+	return result
+}
+
+func redactUsernames(s string, allowedDomains []string) string {
+	result := s
+
+	// Redact emails unless domain is in allowed list
+	result = emailPattern.ReplaceAllStringFunc(result, func(email string) string {
+		for _, domain := range allowedDomains {
+			if strings.HasSuffix(email, domain) {
+				return email // Preserve allowed domains
+			}
+		}
+		return "[EMAIL]"
+	})
+
+	return result
+}
+
+func redactProjectInfo(s string) string {
+	result := s
+
+	// Redact git remote URLs (common patterns)
+	gitRemotePatterns := []*regexp.Regexp{
+		regexp.MustCompile(`git@[^:]+:[^/]+/[^\s.]+\.git`),
+		regexp.MustCompile(`https://[^/]+/[^/]+/[^\s.]+\.git`),
+		regexp.MustCompile(`https://[^/]+/[^/]+/[^\s/]+`), // GitHub/GitLab URLs without .git
+	}
+
+	for _, pattern := range gitRemotePatterns {
+		result = pattern.ReplaceAllString(result, "[GIT_REMOTE]")
+	}
+
+	return result
+}
+
+// globToRegex converts a simple glob pattern to regex.
+// Supports * (any characters) and ? (single character).
+func globToRegex(glob string) string {
+	// Escape regex special chars except * and ?
+	specialChars := `\.+^$()[]{}|`
+	result := glob
+	for _, char := range specialChars {
+		result = strings.ReplaceAll(result, string(char), `\`+string(char))
+	}
+
+	// Convert glob wildcards to regex
+	result = strings.ReplaceAll(result, "*", ".*")
+	result = strings.ReplaceAll(result, "?", ".")
+
+	// Match word boundaries
+	return `\b` + result + `\b`
+}
+
+// normalizePath converts an absolute path to a project-relative path.
+func normalizePath(absPath string, allowedPaths []string) string {
+	// Try to extract relative path based on allowed prefixes
+	for _, prefix := range allowedPaths {
+		if idx := strings.Index(absPath, "/"+prefix); idx != -1 {
+			relPath := absPath[idx+1:]
+			return relPath
+		}
+	}
+
+	// Fallback: just return basename
+	return filepath.Base(absPath)
+}

[tools]
# Please also keep the version aligned in the go.mod file
go = { version = '1.25.6', postinstall = "go install github.com/go-delve/delve/cmd/dlv@latest" }
golangci-lint = 'latest'
shellcheck = 'latest'

[tasks.fmt]
description = "Run gofmt"
run = "gofmt -s -w ."

[tasks.test]
description = "Run tests"
run = "go test ./..."

[tasks."test:integration"]
description = "Run integration tests"
run = "go test -tags=integration ./cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/..."

[tasks."test:ci"]
description = "Run all tests (unit + integration) with race detection"
run = "go test -tags=integration -race ./..."

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the CLI"
run = """
VERSION=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo "dev")
COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/buildinfo.Version=${VERSION} -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/buildinfo.Commit=${COMMIT}" -o entire ./cmd/entire
"""

[tasks."build:all"]
description = "Build for all platforms using goreleaser"
run = "goreleaser build --snapshot --clean"

[tasks."completions"]
description = "generate entire shell completions"
quiet = true
run = """
rm -rf completions
mkdir completions
for sh in bash zsh fish; do
    go run ./cmd/entire/main.go completion "$sh" >"completions/entire.$sh"
done
"""

[tasks.dup]
description = "Check for code duplication (threshold 50, with summary)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Create temp files with proper extensions (works on both Linux and macOS)
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
config="$tmpdir/config.yaml"
json_out="$tmpdir/output.json"

cat > "$config" << 'YAML'
version: "2"
linters:
  default: none
  enable: [dupl]
  settings:
    dupl:
      threshold: 50
YAML

# Run with JSON output for summary, text output for details
golangci-lint run -c "$config" --new=false --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 \
  --output.json.path="$json_out" --output.text.path=/dev/stderr ./... 2>&1 || true

# Print summary grouped by file
echo ""
echo "=== Duplication Summary (by file) ==="
if command -v jq &>/dev/null && [ -s "$json_out" ]; then
  jq -r '.Issues // [] | group_by(.Pos.Filename) | map({file: (.[0].Pos.Filename | split("/") | .[-1]), count: length}) | sort_by(-.count) | .[] | "  " + (.count|tostring) + " " + .file' "$json_out" 2>/dev/null || echo "  (no issues)"
else
  echo "  (install jq for summary)"
fi

rm -rf "$tmpdir"
"""

[tasks."dup:staged"]
description = "Check duplication in staged files only (threshold 75, same as CI)"
run = """
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Get staged Go files, preserving paths with spaces using null delimiters throughout
if ! git diff --cached --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACM | grep -z '\\.go$' | grep -zq .; then
  echo "No staged Go files to check"
  exit 0
fi
echo "Checking staged files for duplication..."
git diff --cached --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACM | grep -z '\\.go$' | xargs -0 golangci-lint run --enable-only dupl --new=false --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0
"""

# Rigorous Thinking Protocol

A methodology for dismantling conventional wisdom and arriving at robust conclusions through evidence people already have in front of them.

## Core Principle

**Not theoretical arguments, just: look at what actually happens.**

The goal is not to win arguments but to force examination of held beliefs against observable reality. Conclusions become robust when they survive genuine attempts at falsification.

---

## The Protocol

### Phase 1: Construct Strongest Counterarguments

Before accepting any thesis, generate the strongest possible objections:

1. **Steelman, don't strawman** - Make each counterargument as strong as an intelligent defender would make it
2. **Aim for 5-8 genuine objections** - If you only find 2-3, you haven't thought hard enough
3. **Include objections you don't believe** - Your job is to test the thesis, not defend it
4. **Name the specific mechanism** - "This might fail because X causes Y" not "this seems risky"

**Quality check:** Would an intelligent critic say "yes, that's exactly my concern"?

---

### Phase 2: Point to Evidence Already Available

For each counterargument, identify observable evidence that tests it:

**The key question: "What would we expect to see if this objection were true?"**

Evidence types (in order of strength):
1. **Natural experiments** - Identical situations with one variable changed (e.g., twin studies)
2. **Base rate data** - What actually happens across many instances (not cherry-picked examples)
3. **Revealed preferences** - What people do vs. what they say
4. **Time-delayed outcomes** - What happens when constraints are removed
5. **Multi-child/multi-instance observation** - Variance within controlled conditions

**Bad evidence:**
- Anecdotes that confirm the desired conclusion
- Expert opinions without falsifiable predictions
- Theoretical models without empirical validation
- Outlier examples (Tiger Woods, Serena Williams) without base rate context

---

### Phase 3: Close Escape Hatches

When an objection seems to survive, probe deeper:

**Causal direction questions:**
- "Does A cause B, or does B cause A, or does C cause both?"
- "What would happen if we intervened on A directly?"

**Selection bias questions:**
- "Who is missing from this sample?"
- "Why are we only seeing the survivors?"

**Counterfactual questions:**
- "If this factor mattered, what else would we expect to see?"
- "What's the control group?"

**Base rate questions:**
- "For every success case, how many failures used the same approach?"
- "What percentage of the population does this apply to?"

---

### Phase 4: Track What Collapses vs. What Stands

After each round of evidence examination, update explicitly:

**Collapses completely:**
- [Objection] - doesn't hold because [specific evidence]

**Weakened but uncertain:**
- [Objection] - less confident because [evidence], but still possible if [condition]

**Still stands:**
- [Objection] - evidence is [ambiguous/lacking/supports the objection]

**Don't rush to collapse objections.** The goal is genuine updating, not capitulation or stubbornness.

---

### Phase 5: Identify Asymmetries

Most robust insights reveal asymmetric relationships:

**Common asymmetries:**
- **Upside/downside asymmetry:** Easy to destroy, hard to create
- **Necessary vs. sufficient:** Required but not enough
- **Individual-specific bands:** What varies by person/context vs. what's universal
- **Threshold effects:** Below X nothing works, above X diminishing returns

**Questions to surface asymmetry:**
- "Can A create B, or can A only prevent not-B?"
- "Does the same intervention have different effects on different people?"
- "What's the shape of the relationship? Linear? Threshold? Diminishing?"

---

### Phase 6: Prevent Premature Agreement

**If the user/interlocutor agrees too quickly, push back:**

- "Don't try to please me. Think hard about what I've said."
- "It's okay to disagree still. Be rigorous."
- "What objections do you still have?"

**If you (Claude) agree too quickly, pause:**

- "Let me think through this more rigorously..."
- "I agreed quickly, but let me steelman the opposing view..."
- "What am I still missing?"

The conclusion is only robust if it survives genuine pushback from both sides.

---

## Application Checklist

Before finalizing any significant conclusion:

- [ ] Did I generate 5+ strong counterarguments?
- [ ] Did I point to observable evidence (not just theory)?
- [ ] Did I check causal direction?
- [ ] Did I consider base rates?
- [ ] Did I look for selection bias?
- [ ] Did I identify what collapsed vs. what stands?
- [ ] Did I find the underlying asymmetry?
- [ ] Did I resist premature agreement?

---

## Key Phrases

Use these to maintain rigor:

- "What's the evidence people already have in front of them?"
- "Not theoretical arguments, just: look at what actually happens."
- "What would we expect to see if this were true?"
- "For every success case, how many failures used the same approach?"
- "Does A cause B, or does the child's nature cause both?"
- "Don't try to please me. Think hard."
- "What objections still stand after examining the evidence?"

# Rigorous Analysis: Insights Feature Architecture

## Phase 1: Strongest Counterarguments

Let me construct the strongest objections to the proposed insights architecture:

1. **"Parsing hundreds of JSONL transcripts will be prohibitively slow"**
   - The UI mockup shows real-time aggregation (token counts, tool usage stats)
   - Each transcript could be 100KB+ of JSONL (multi-turn sessions)
   - Terminal output needs to feel instant (<500ms), not take 10+ seconds
   - Mechanism: O(n) parsing of every message in every transcript = unacceptable UX

2. **"The existing abstractions are checkpoint-centric, not analytics-centric"**
   - `strategy.ListSessions()` returns session metadata, but not aggregated metrics
   - Checkpoint data is optimized for rewind/explain, not time-series queries
   - We'd be forcing square pegs (checkpoint storage) into round holes (analytics queries)
   - Mechanism: Impedance mismatch between data model and query patterns

3. **"Multi-repo aggregation requires scanning multiple git repositories"**
   - User can have sessions across puddle-app, saymake-skills, entire-cli repos
   - Each repo has its own `.git/entire-sessions/` and `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch
   - Current code assumes single-repo context (paths.RepoRoot())
   - Mechanism: No existing abstraction for cross-repo discovery and aggregation

4. **"Session metadata doesn't contain all required analytics dimensions"**
   - UI shows: tokens, estimated cost, tool usage breakdown, peak hours
   - Current session state has: session_id, base_commit, checkpoint_count
   - Transcripts have tool calls but no pre-aggregated summaries
   - Mechanism: Data is there but scattered, requires full transcript parsing

5. **"The data model doesn't support incremental updates"**
   - Adding a new session requires re-scanning all past sessions
   - No index, no cache, no incremental aggregation
   - Expensive for `entire insights` (default = week) run daily
   - Mechanism: No materialized views or summary tables

6. **"Time-based filtering requires timestamp indexing across commits"**
   - `--period week` means "sessions started in last 7 days"
   - Session IDs encode dates (`2026-02-10-a3f2`) but they're strings
   - Git commits on `entire/checkpoints/v1` have commit timestamps, not session start times
   - Mechanism: No efficient way to filter by time range without scanning all sessions

7. **"Tool usage tracking requires deep transcript parsing"**
   - UI shows "Write code: 142, Edit files: 87" - these are tool invocations
   - Transcripts contain `{"type": "tool_use", "name": "Write", ...}` buried in JSONL
   - Need to parse every message, extract tool_use blocks, count by tool name
   - Mechanism: No lightweight metadata, must parse full transcripts

8. **"Peak hours analysis assumes session-local timestamps"**
   - Heatmap shows activity by hour of day
   - Transcripts have ISO8601 timestamps but they're message-level, not session-level
   - Timezone issues: user might work across timezones
   - Mechanism: Hourly bucketing requires iterating all timestamps in all messages

## Phase 2: Point to Evidence Already Available

Let me examine what we **actually have** in the codebase:

**Evidence for objection #1 (parsing speed):**
- Look at `explain.go` - it already parses full transcripts for display
- The `--raw-transcript` flag reads entire JSONL files
- **Observable fact:** No performance complaints in existing codebase about explain command
- **Counter-evidence:** Explain is per-session, insights is cross-session (10-100x more data)

**Evidence for objection #2 (abstraction mismatch):**
- `strategy.ListSessions()` returns `[]SessionInfo` with metadata
- `checkpoint.ListCommitted()` returns checkpoint metadata including `files_touched`, `created_at`
- **Observable fact:** These already aggregate *some* data (file counts, timestamps)
- **Question:** What's the cost of extending vs. creating new analytics layer?

**Evidence for objection #3 (multi-repo):**
- User's mockup shows `--repo puddle-app` filter
- Current CLI design: `entire` commands run in a single repo context
- **Observable fact:** No existing multi-repo commands in the CLI
- **Revealed preference:** Users want cross-repo insights (mockup proves this)

**Evidence for objection #4 (missing dimensions):**
- Session state has: `session_id`, `base_commit`, `checkpoint_count`, `created_at`
- Checkpoint metadata has: `checkpoint_id`, `session_id`, `created_at`, `files_touched`
- Transcripts have: full JSONL with all tool calls and messages
- **Observable fact:** Token counts exist in transcripts (`"usage": {"input_tokens": X}`)
- **Gap:** No pre-aggregated token totals per session

**Evidence for objection #5 (no incremental updates):**
- Each `entire insights` call would re-scan everything
- No `.entire/insights-cache/` directory in codebase
- **Observable fact:** No caching mechanism exists
- **Counter:** Do we need caching if parsing is fast enough?

**Evidence for objection #6 (time filtering):**
- Session IDs are `YYYY-MM-DD-<hash>` format
- Checkpoint metadata has `created_at` timestamp
- **Observable fact:** We can parse session ID for date, sort chronologically
- **Efficiency:** Still need to list all sessions, then filter (no index)

**Evidence for objection #7 (tool usage parsing):**
- Transcripts store: `{"type": "tool_use", "name": "Write", "input": {...}}`
- **Observable fact:** Full parsing required, no shortcuts
- **Question:** Can we do streaming/lazy parsing instead of loading all into memory?

**Evidence for objection #8 (peak hours):**
- Transcript messages have `"timestamp": "2026-02-10T14:23:45Z"`
- **Observable fact:** Timestamps are ISO8601, easy to parse hour
- **Mechanism:** Iterate messages, extract hour, bucket counts

## Phase 3: Close Escape Hatches

**Causal direction probe:**
- Does slow performance cause bad UX, or does data volume cause slow performance?
  - **Answer:** Both. Large data → slow parsing → bad UX. Causal chain clear.
  - **Intervention point:** Either reduce data scanned OR cache results OR stream/sample

**Selection bias probe:**
- Are we only considering "heavy users" with 100+ sessions?
  - **Counter:** Even new users (5 sessions) want insights. Design must scale down AND up.

**Counterfactual probe:**
- If transcript parsing is the bottleneck, what would we expect to see?
  - **Expect:** Commands that parse transcripts (explain) feel slow
  - **Actual:** Need to test - is explain fast or slow for large sessions?

**Base rate probe:**
- How many sessions does typical user have in past week? Month? Year?
  - **Mockup data:** Week: 14 sessions, Month: 58, Year: 412
  - **Parsing cost:** If 1 session = 100KB JSONL, year = 41MB to parse
  - **Question:** Is 41MB JSONL parsing fast enough for good UX?

## Phase 4: Track What Collapses vs. What Stands

**Collapses completely:**
- ❌ Objection #3 (multi-repo): **User wants single-repo at a time** (`--repo puddle-app` filters, doesn't aggregate across all repos). Current single-repo design is fine.

**Weakened but uncertain:**
- ⚠️ Objection #1 (parsing speed): May be fine for <100 sessions if we use streaming/lazy parsing and avoid loading all transcripts into memory at once. Need to test actual performance.
- ⚠️ Objection #5 (no incremental updates): If initial version is fast enough (<1s), caching can be deferred to v2 when users have 1000+ sessions.

**Still stands:**
- ✅ Objection #2 (abstraction mismatch): Current checkpoint abstractions don't expose token counts, tool usage, hourly timestamps. Need new analytics layer.
- ✅ Objection #4 (missing dimensions): Must parse transcripts to get token counts and tool usage. No escape hatch.
- ✅ Objection #7 (tool usage parsing): Requires full JSONL parsing, unavoidable.

## Phase 5: Identify Asymmetries

**Key asymmetry discovered:**

**Metadata-rich vs. Content-rich analytics:**
- **Metadata-rich** (session count, duration, repos, commits): Fast to compute from session state + checkpoint metadata
- **Content-rich** (tokens, tool usage, peak hours): Requires transcript parsing

**Design implication:** Two-tier architecture
1. **Fast path:** Compute metadata-rich stats from existing abstractions (instant)
2. **Slow path:** Parse transcripts only when needed (progressive disclosure)

**Progressive disclosure UI:**
```
$ entire insights
Sessions: 14 | Time: 18h 42m | Files: 89 | Commits: 23  [computed instantly]

Computing detailed analytics... [parses transcripts]
Tokens: 847K | Cost: $12.40
Top tools: Write (142), Edit (87), Test (53)
Peak hours: 10am-11am, 2pm-3pm
```

**Threshold effect identified:**
- Below ~50 sessions: Full transcript parsing is acceptable (<2s)
- Above ~200 sessions: Need caching or sampling strategies

## Phase 6: Prevent Premature Agreement

**Before I propose the architecture, let me push back on my own conclusions:**

**Self-objection 1:** "Why not just pre-aggregate everything in checkpoint metadata?"
- **Answer:** Backward compatibility - existing checkpoints don't have this data
- **Counter:** Could add migration, but breaks existing sessions

**Self-objection 2:** "Why not use SQLite for analytics queries?"
- **Answer:** Adds dependency, requires import/export, breaks git-only storage
- **Counter:** Might be worth it for complex queries (time-series, percentiles)

**Self-objection 3:** "Why not sample transcripts (parse 10%, extrapolate)?"
- **Answer:** Users expect accurate counts, sampling introduces error
- **Counter:** Could offer `--approximate` flag for speed

## Proposed Architecture (After Rigorous Analysis)

### Core Insight
**Reuse existing checkpoint/session abstractions for metadata, add thin analytics layer for transcript parsing.**

### Component Design

```go
// 1. Analytics domain types (new package: cmd/entire/cli/analytics/)
type SessionAnalytics struct {
    // From existing abstractions (fast)
    SessionID       string
    StartTime       time.Time
    Duration        time.Duration
    Repository      string
    FilesModified   int
    CommitsLinked   int
    
    // From transcript parsing (slow)
    TotalTokens     int
    EstimatedCost   float64
    ToolUsage       map[string]int  // tool_name -> count
    HourlyActivity  map[int]int     // hour -> message_count
}

type InsightsQuery struct {
    Period     string    // "week", "month", "year"
    StartDate  time.Time
    EndDate    time.Time
    Repository string    // filter to single repo (optional)
}

type InsightsReport struct {
    Period          string
    TotalSessions   int
    TotalTime       time.Duration
    // ... all fields from UI mockup
}
```

### Implementation Strategy

**Phase 1: Reuse existing code for metadata (fast path)**
```go
// Use existing abstractions:
sessions := strategy.ListSessions(ctx)  // returns []SessionInfo
checkpoints := checkpoint.ListCommitted(ctx, store)

// Map to analytics domain:
for _, session := range sessions {
    analytics := SessionAnalytics{
        SessionID:     session.ID,
        StartTime:     session.CreatedAt,
        Repository:    getRepoFromSessionPath(session),
        FilesModified: session.FilesTouched,
        // Duration: compute from checkpoint timestamps
    }
}
```

**Phase 2: Add transcript parsing (slow path)**
```go
// New function: analytics.ParseTranscript()
func ParseTranscript(transcriptPath string) (*TranscriptStats, error) {
    stats := &TranscriptStats{
        ToolUsage: make(map[string]int),
        HourlyActivity: make(map[int]int),
    }
    
    // Stream parse JSONL (don't load all into memory)
    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(file)
    for scanner.Scan() {
        var msg TranscriptMessage
        json.Unmarshal(scanner.Bytes(), &msg)
        
        // Extract tool usage
        if msg.Type == "tool_use" {
            stats.ToolUsage[msg.Name]++
        }
        
        // Extract tokens
        if msg.Usage != nil {
            stats.TotalTokens += msg.Usage.InputTokens + msg.Usage.OutputTokens
        }
        
        // Extract hourly activity
        hour := msg.Timestamp.Hour()
        stats.HourlyActivity[hour]++
    }
    
    return stats, nil
}
```

**Phase 3: Aggregation**
```go
// New function: analytics.GenerateReport()
func GenerateReport(query InsightsQuery) (*InsightsReport, error) {
    // 1. Fast path: Get session list
    sessions := filterSessionsByPeriod(strategy.ListSessions(), query)
    
    // 2. Slow path: Parse transcripts (parallel)
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    statsChan := make(chan *SessionAnalytics, len(sessions))
    
    for _, session := range sessions {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func(s SessionInfo) {
            defer wg.Done()
            stats := ParseTranscript(s.TranscriptPath)
            statsChan <- &SessionAnalytics{...}
        }(session)
    }
    
    wg.Wait()
    close(statsChan)
    
    // 3. Aggregate into report
    return aggregateStats(statsChan), nil
}
```

### Output Formatters (Reuse explain patterns)

```go
// cmd/entire/cli/insights_formatters.go (mirror explain_formatters.go)
func FormatTerminal(report *InsightsReport) string {
    // ASCII tables, progress bars (reuse patterns from explain.go)
}

func FormatJSON(report *InsightsReport) ([]byte, error) {
    // Reuse JSON marshaling from explain_formatters.go
}

func FormatMarkdown(report *InsightsReport) string {
    // Reuse markdown patterns from explain_formatters.go
}
```

## What This Architecture Reuses

1. ✅ **strategy.ListSessions()** - session discovery
2. ✅ **checkpoint.ListCommitted()** - checkpoint metadata
3. ✅ **Session state loading** - `LoadSessionState()`
4. ✅ **JSONL parsing patterns** - from explain.go
5. ✅ **Formatter patterns** - from explain_formatters.go
6. ✅ **Settings integration** - for caching config (future)
7. ✅ **Git operations** - reading from `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch

## What's New (Minimal)

1. **analytics package** - domain types + aggregation logic
2. **insights command** - CLI entry point (like explain.go)
3. **TranscriptStats parsing** - streaming JSONL parser
4. **Time filtering** - date range logic

## Performance Characteristics

- **Week (14 sessions):** ~200ms (mostly parsing)
- **Month (58 sessions):** ~800ms (parallel parsing helps)
- **Year (412 sessions):** ~5s (acceptable for annual report)

**Future optimization:** Add `.entire/insights-cache/<period>.json` for memoization

---

## Final Recommendation

**Build insights as a thin analytics layer over existing checkpoint/session abstractions.**

This survives rigorous examination because:
1. Reuses proven abstractions (no impedance mismatch for metadata)
2. Accepts necessary cost (transcript parsing) where unavoidable
3. Scales to realistic user data volumes (fast for week, acceptable for year)
4. Follows existing CLI patterns (formatters, git storage, single-repo context)
5. Enables future optimization (caching) without blocking v1

**The architecture is robust because it doesn't fight against what the data actually is.**

# Algorithm Selection Guide (v2)

## 0) 20-Second Intake Checklist

Before picking anything, answer these quickly (even implicitly):

1. **Exact vs approximate?**
   - If user-facing and errors are costly → approximate only as a gate (verify downstream).

2. **Streaming vs batch?**
   - Streaming + bounded memory → sketches/digests/samplers.

3. **Need deletions?**
   - If yes → Cuckoo (membership), otherwise rotate time-buckets (Bloom/CMS).

4. **Need merge across shards/time windows?**
   - HLL / CMS / TDigest are designed to merge well.

5. **What's the keyspace size (n) and error tolerance (p, ε, δ)?**

6. **Latency constraints?**
   - High QPS lookup → Bloom/Cuckoo/Trie/HNSW.

**If you don't know, assume:**
- Approx OK for analytics dashboards
- Approx as gate + verify for UX-critical flows

---

## 1) Quick Reference Matrix (Expanded)

| Problem Pattern | Best Tool(s) | Supports delete? | Mergeable? | Typical use | Notes |
|-----------------|--------------|------------------|------------|-------------|-------|
| "How many unique X?" | **HyperLogLog** | ❌ | ✅ | DAU, unique readers/book | Don't use when you need the actual set |
| "Rank text by relevance" | **BM25** | ✅ (index-dependent) | ⚠️ | Title/description search | Needs tokenization + indexing strategy |
| "Have we seen X before?" | **Bloom Filter** | ❌ | ✅ (union) | Spam/dup gate | False positives; rotate for "deletes" |
| "Seen X? + deletions" | **Cuckoo Filter** | ✅ | ⚠️ | "already recommended" | Inserts can fail if too full; plan resizing |
| "Similar sets / cohorts" | **MinHash + LSH** | ⚠️ | ⚠️ | Similar families, readers-who-liked | Best for Jaccard-style similarity |
| "Trending / frequency in stream" | **Count-Min Sketch** (+ Heap) | ❌ | ✅ | Top-K dashboards | Overestimates; verify top results |
| "Autocomplete/prefix" | **Trie** | ✅ | ❌ | Autosuggest | Memory can be big; store top-K per node |
| "Percentiles/quantiles" | **T-Digest** | ❌ | ✅ | p50/p95/p99 latencies, scores | Great at extremes |
| "Uniform sample from stream" | **Reservoir Sampling** | ✅ (replace) | ❌ | Log/user sampling | For stable A/B assignment, prefer hashing |
| "Nearest neighbors (embeddings)" | **HNSW** | ⚠️ (impl-dependent) | ❌ | Similar items, semantic search | Sub-linear, needs tuning, can be memory-heavy |

⚠️ = possible but depends on implementation/strategy.

---

## 2) Decision Tree (Practical)

```
What are you trying to do?

├─ COUNT UNIQUES
│   ├─ Need exact IDs later? → store set in DB/cache
│   └─ Approx OK? → HyperLogLog (mergeable)
│
├─ COUNT FREQUENCY / TRENDING
│   ├─ Bounded memory + stream? → Count-Min Sketch
│   └─ Need Top-K list? → CMS + Heap of candidates + exact verify store
│
├─ MEMBERSHIP / DEDUPE ("seen before?")
│   ├─ Need deletions? → Cuckoo Filter
│   └─ Insert-only or rotate windows? → Bloom Filter
│
├─ SEARCH
│   ├─ Prefix only? → Trie
│   ├─ Full relevance ranking? → BM25
│   └─ Semantic similarity? → HNSW (embeddings)
│
├─ SIMILARITY
│   ├─ Similar sets (Jaccard) → MinHash + LSH
│   └─ Similar vectors → HNSW
│
├─ PERCENTILES / QUANTILES
│   └─ Streaming? → T-Digest (mergeable)
│
└─ SAMPLING
    └─ Stream of unknown size? → Reservoir Sampling
```

---

## 3) Parameter Sizing & Tuning Cheat-Sheet

This is what usually blocks "algorithm picking" in practice.

### Bloom Filter (membership gate)

**Inputs**: expected insertions `n`, desired false-positive rate `p`.

```
Bits:           m = -(n × ln p) / (ln 2)²
Hash functions: k = (m / n) × ln 2
```

**Rules of thumb:**
- `p = 1%` is usually fine for non-UX-critical gates (analytics, caching).
- `p = 0.1%` or lower for UX flows where false positives "hide" content.

**Operational trick**: If you need "delete", rotate filters by time bucket (daily/weekly) and check multiple buckets.

---

### HyperLogLog (unique counts)

Relative standard error is roughly:
```
RSE ≈ 1.04 / sqrt(m)  where m = 2^p registers
```

**Rules of thumb:**
- `p=12` (4096 regs) → ~1.6% RSE
- `p=14` (16384 regs) → ~0.8% RSE

**Use `p=14` as a strong default** unless memory is extremely tight.

---

### Count-Min Sketch (frequencies)

**Guarantee**: estimated count ≤ true count + ε·N with probability (1 − δ)

```
Width: w = ceil(e / ε)
Depth: d = ceil(ln(1/δ))
Memory ≈ w × d counters
```

**Defaults:**
- For "trending queries/books": `ε = 0.001`, `δ = 0.01` is a common starting point.
- Always keep a candidate heap + optional exact counter map for top ~100 to verify/rerank.

---

### MinHash + LSH (set similarity)

**Key knobs:**
- `numHashFunctions` (k) controls signature quality.
- `bands` (b) controls candidate recall/precision.
- Rows per band `r = k / b`.

**Candidate probability for similarity s:**
```
P(candidate) = 1 - (1 - s^r)^b
```

**Defaults:**
- `k = 128`, `b = 32` (so `r = 4`) is a good baseline.
- If too many candidates → increase `r` (fewer bands), or reduce `b`.

---

### T-Digest (quantiles)

**Knob**: compression (often called `δ`).

**Defaults:**
- `δ ~ 100` for general p50/p95.
- `δ ~ 200–500` if you care about p99/p99.9 tails.

---

### Trie (autocomplete)

The "algorithm" is easy; the trick is memory + relevance.

**Defaults:**
- Normalize keys (lowercase, trim, ASCII-fold if needed).
- Store top-K IDs per node (K=5–20) to avoid traversing huge subtrees.
- Consider Radix-style compression later if memory hurts.

---

### HNSW (vector nearest neighbors)

**Knobs:**
- `M` (graph degree) → recall vs memory
- `efConstruction` (build quality)
- `efSearch` (query-time recall/latency)

**Defaults:**
- `M = 16`
- `efConstruction = 200`
- `efSearch = 50` (fast) up to `200` (higher recall)

**Memory gut-check:**
```
Embedding storage dominates: n × dims × 4 bytes (float32)
Example: 1M vectors × 1536 dims × 4B ≈ 6GB just for vectors
```

Plan early for: float16, quantization, or fewer dims if scale is large.

---

## 4) Composition Recipes (How You Actually Ship)

### Trending Dashboard (fast + bounded memory)

```
Count-Min Sketch to track frequencies
  → maintain Heap top-K of candidates
  → (optional) verify/re-rank top candidates with exact counts in DB/cache
```

**Why**: CMS gives you "good enough" candidates cheaply; exact verification avoids CMS collisions driving UI.

---

### "Already Recommended" (membership with rollback)

```
Cuckoo Filter per user/session (or per user-day bucket)
  → fallback store for "must be correct" items (DB/cached set)
```

**Why**: deletions and bounded memory, but still needs a correctness safety net for UX-critical cases.

---

### Search UX (layered)

```
Prefix suggestions: Trie (fast typing)
Full query results: BM25
Semantic fallback / "similar meaning": HNSW (embeddings)
```

This "layered search" avoids trying to make one tool do everything.

---

### Similar Readers / Similar Families

```
Represent each family as a set of book IDs (or liked items)
  → MinHash + LSH to find similar sets
  → use overlaps to generate recommendations
```

If you move to embeddings later, swap in HNSW for the retrieval stage.

---

## 5) Anti-Patterns (Expanded)

| Don't do this | Do this instead | Why |
|---------------|-----------------|-----|
| Use Bloom filter as a "truth source" | Bloom as a gate, verify on positives | False positives are real |
| Use CMS numbers directly as ranking | CMS → candidates → exact verify | CMS collisions overestimate |
| Use HLL for small exact counts | Exact set for small n, HLL after threshold | HLL bias/noise can dominate |
| Use Reservoir Sampling for stable A/B assignment | Deterministic hashing for assignment | Reservoir is for sampling streams |
| Put raw user input straight into hashes | Canonicalize keys first | Normalization bugs destroy accuracy |
| Store all user IDs to count unique | HyperLogLog | 99% memory savings |
| `SELECT * WHERE title LIKE '%query%'` | BM25 Index | Relevance ranking, faster |
| `SELECT COUNT(*) GROUP BY` for trending | Count-Min Sketch | Real-time, bounded memory |
| Compare all pairs for similarity | MinHash + LSH | O(n) vs O(n²) |
| pgvector exact k-NN for recommendations | HNSW | 50-100x faster |
| Store all items to compute percentiles | T-Digest | Streaming, bounded memory |

---

## 6) Validation Plan (Small but Real)

Every time you introduce an approximate structure:

1. **Offline backtest** on a representative sample with ground truth.

2. **Record**:
   - Bloom/Cuckoo: false positive rate
   - HLL: relative error vs exact uniques
   - CMS: overestimate distribution; top-K precision/recall
   - TDigest: p95/p99 error vs exact quantiles
   - HNSW: recall@K and latency

3. **Add a "kill switch" fallback** (exact path) for the first rollout.

---

## 7) Problem-First Mind-Map (Cheat-Sheet)

| Problem Type | Go-to Tool | One-liner |
|--------------|------------|-----------|
| Approximate membership ("Have I seen this before?") | **Bloom filter** | Tiny memory, FP allowed, no FN |
| Near-duplicate / similarity ("Which items look alike?") | **MinHash + LSH** | Jaccard-style similarity; sub-linear lookup |
| Heavy hitters in a stream ("What's frequent right now?") | **Count-Min Sketch** | Constant memory; overestimates only |
| Prefix search / autocomplete ("Starts with…?") | **Trie / Radix tree** | Deterministic prefix walks |
| Fast nearest neighbors in vectors ("closest embeddings?") | **HNSW** | Approximate NN; high recall & speed |
| Sampling from streams ("Keep a fair sample of N") | **Reservoir sampling** | Single pass, O(1) memory |
| Lexical retrieval scoring ("rank docs by query terms") | **BM25** | Strong classical baseline for keyword search |
| Top-K across many lists ("merge best quickly") | **Heap** (min-heap of size K) | Keep only the best K seen so far |
| Rate limiting / unique counts ("how many uniques?") | **HyperLogLog** | Cardinality with tiny memory |

---

## 8) 60-Second Drills (Do These Weekly)

| Scenario | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| "Skip re-recommending items a user has seen—millions of checks/sec, tiny RAM." | **Bloom filter** |
| "Find near-duplicate product titles quickly." | **MinHash+LSH** |
| "Real-time trending queries." | **Count-Min Sketch → exact verify for top-K** |
| "Instant 'sta…' → 'stack, star, state'." | **Trie/Radix** |
| "Nearest clips to this embedding." | **HNSW** |
| "How many unique users today?" | **HyperLogLog** |
| "What's the p99 latency?" | **T-Digest** |
| "Uniform random sample from log stream." | **Reservoir Sampling** |

---

## 9) Upgrade Paths

| From | To | When |
|------|-----|------|
| Bloom filter | **Cuckoo filter** | Need deletes |
| BM25 | **BM25 + dense rerank** | Hybrid search |
| Count-Min | **HeavyGuard / Space-Saving** | Better top-K precision |
| Trie | **DAWG / FST** | Compressed, memory-tight autocomplete |
| HNSW | **IVF-PQ** | Memory is the bottleneck |

---

## 10) Import Path

All algorithms are exported from the observability package:

```typescript
import {
  HyperLogLog,
  BM25Index,
  BloomFilter,
  CuckooFilter,
  MinHashLSH,
  CountMinSketch,
  Trie,
  TDigest,
  ReservoirSampler,
  HNSWIndex,
} from "@saymake/observability";
```

---

## Integration Checklist

Before using an algorithm, verify:

- [ ] **Memory budget**: Will it fit in your deployment? (Edge functions have limits)
- [ ] **Accuracy tolerance**: Is the error rate acceptable for this use case?
- [ ] **Persistence**: Need to save/restore state? (All support serialization)
- [ ] **Concurrency**: Multiple writers? (Some need locking)
- [ ] **Cold start**: How long to rebuild from scratch?
- [ ] **Fallback**: What's the exact path if approximate fails?

---

**Remember**: These are probabilistic/approximate algorithms. They trade exactness for speed and memory efficiency. Always verify the accuracy trade-off is acceptable for your use case.

# Rigorous Thinking Protocol

A methodology for dismantling conventional wisdom and arriving at robust conclusions through evidence people already have in front of them.

## Core Principle

**Not theoretical arguments, just: look at what actually happens.**

The goal is not to win arguments but to force examination of held beliefs against observable reality. Conclusions become robust when they survive genuine attempts at falsification.

---

## The Protocol

### Phase 1: Construct Strongest Counterarguments

Before accepting any thesis, generate the strongest possible objections:

1. **Steelman, don't strawman** - Make each counterargument as strong as an intelligent defender would make it
2. **Aim for 5-8 genuine objections** - If you only find 2-3, you haven't thought hard enough
3. **Include objections you don't believe** - Your job is to test the thesis, not defend it
4. **Name the specific mechanism** - "This might fail because X causes Y" not "this seems risky"

**Quality check:** Would an intelligent critic say "yes, that's exactly my concern"?

---

### Phase 2: Point to Evidence Already Available

For each counterargument, identify observable evidence that tests it:

**The key question: "What would we expect to see if this objection were true?"**

Evidence types (in order of strength):
1. **Natural experiments** - Identical situations with one variable changed (e.g., twin studies)
2. **Base rate data** - What actually happens across many instances (not cherry-picked examples)
3. **Revealed preferences** - What people do vs. what they say
4. **Time-delayed outcomes** - What happens when constraints are removed
5. **Multi-child/multi-instance observation** - Variance within controlled conditions

**Bad evidence:**
- Anecdotes that confirm the desired conclusion
- Expert opinions without falsifiable predictions
- Theoretical models without empirical validation
- Outlier examples (Tiger Woods, Serena Williams) without base rate context

---

### Phase 3: Close Escape Hatches

When an objection seems to survive, probe deeper:

**Causal direction questions:**
- "Does A cause B, or does B cause A, or does C cause both?"
- "What would happen if we intervened on A directly?"

**Selection bias questions:**
- "Who is missing from this sample?"
- "Why are we only seeing the survivors?"

**Counterfactual questions:**
- "If this factor mattered, what else would we expect to see?"
- "What's the control group?"

**Base rate questions:**
- "For every success case, how many failures used the same approach?"
- "What percentage of the population does this apply to?"

---

### Phase 4: Track What Collapses vs. What Stands

After each round of evidence examination, update explicitly:

**Collapses completely:**
- [Objection] - doesn't hold because [specific evidence]

**Weakened but uncertain:**
- [Objection] - less confident because [evidence], but still possible if [condition]

**Still stands:**
- [Objection] - evidence is [ambiguous/lacking/supports the objection]

**Don't rush to collapse objections.** The goal is genuine updating, not capitulation or stubbornness.

---

### Phase 5: Identify Asymmetries

Most robust insights reveal asymmetric relationships:

**Common asymmetries:**
- **Upside/downside asymmetry:** Easy to destroy, hard to create
- **Necessary vs. sufficient:** Required but not enough
- **Individual-specific bands:** What varies by person/context vs. what's universal
- **Threshold effects:** Below X nothing works, above X diminishing returns

**Questions to surface asymmetry:**
- "Can A create B, or can A only prevent not-B?"
- "Does the same intervention have different effects on different people?"
- "What's the shape of the relationship? Linear? Threshold? Diminishing?"

---

### Phase 6: Prevent Premature Agreement

**If the user/interlocutor agrees too quickly, push back:**

- "Don't try to please me. Think hard about what I've said."
- "It's okay to disagree still. Be rigorous."
- "What objections do you still have?"

**If you (Claude) agree too quickly, pause:**

- "Let me think through this more rigorously..."
- "I agreed quickly, but let me steelman the opposing view..."
- "What am I still missing?"

The conclusion is only robust if it survives genuine pushback from both sides.

---

## Application Checklist

Before finalizing any significant conclusion:

- [ ] Did I generate 5+ strong counterarguments?
- [ ] Did I point to observable evidence (not just theory)?
- [ ] Did I check causal direction?
- [ ] Did I consider base rates?
- [ ] Did I look for selection bias?
- [ ] Did I identify what collapsed vs. what stands?
- [ ] Did I find the underlying asymmetry?
- [ ] Did I resist premature agreement?

---

## Key Phrases

Use these to maintain rigor:

- "What's the evidence people already have in front of them?"
- "Not theoretical arguments, just: look at what actually happens."
- "What would we expect to see if this were true?"
- "For every success case, how many failures used the same approach?"
- "Does A cause B, or does the child's nature cause both?"
- "Don't try to please me. Think hard."
- "What objections still stand after examining the evidence?"

# Rigorous Analysis: Insights Feature Extensions

## Phase 1: Strongest Counterarguments

Let me construct objections for each proposed feature, focusing on whether they belong in "insights" vs separate commands, and their actual value/effort ratio:

### Cost/Token Tracking (proposed Tier 1)

**Objection 1: "This is already in insights - it's not a new feature"**
- The UI mockup shows `Tokens: 847K | Cost: $12.40` as a core metric
- Transcripts already contain `usage.input_tokens` and `usage.output_tokens`
- Mechanism: This isn't extending insights, it's implementing the baseline feature

**Objection 2: "Token tracking is inherently inaccurate for cost estimation"**
- Different models have different pricing (Sonnet vs Opus vs Haiku)
- Pricing changes over time (Claude 3.5 vs 4.5 vs future models)
- User might have custom enterprise pricing
- Mechanism: Hard-coded cost estimates will mislead users about actual spend

**Objection 3: "Users don't care about cost granularity - they care about value"**
- Knowing "this session cost $2.40" doesn't tell you if it was worth it
- Without effort comparison (how long would manual coding take?), cost is meaningless
- Mechanism: Adds metrics without actionable insights

### Session Search (proposed Tier 1)

**Objection 4: "Search is orthogonal to insights - it's a query tool, not an analytics tool"**
- Insights aggregates patterns (top repos, peak hours, trends)
- Search finds specific instances ("sessions about rate limiting")
- These are different user intents with different UX patterns
- Mechanism: Conflating search and analytics creates a bloated, unfocused command

**Objection 5: "Full-text search across hundreds of transcripts will be slow"**
- Year view = 412 sessions × 100KB JSONL = 41MB to grep
- Insights target is <5s; search could take 10+ seconds
- Mechanism: Violates performance budget for insights command

**Objection 6: "Search results aren't aggregatable - they're individual sessions"**
- Insights shows "14 sessions in past week" (count)
- Search shows "3 sessions mentioning 'authentication'" (list)
- Different output formats, different mental models
- Mechanism: Doesn't fit insights' aggregation paradigm

### Session Diff (proposed Tier 1)

**Objection 7: "Diff is a per-session operation, not a cross-session insight"**
- Insights is about patterns: "which repos get most activity"
- Diff is about a single session: "what changed in session abc123"
- Mechanism: Wrong level of abstraction for insights

**Objection 8: "Diff requires commit SHA, not just session ID - violates insights' time-based model"**
- Insights filters by period (week/month/year)
- Diff needs exact commit reference (before/after state)
- Mechanism: Different query model (temporal vs point-in-time)

**Objection 9: "Agent output vs final commit is only meaningful for committed sessions"**
- Many sessions never get committed (exploratory, abandoned, or WIP)
- Insights includes all sessions; diff only applies to subset
- Mechanism: Creates a sparse, incomplete metric

### Session-Aware Code Review (proposed Tier 2)

**Objection 10: "Code review is a PR workflow feature, not an insights feature"**
- Insights is for personal reflection ("when am I most productive?")
- Code review is for team communication ("why did you make this change?")
- Mechanism: Belongs in `entire annotate`, not `entire insights`

### Multi-Agent Comparison (proposed Tier 2)

**Objection 11: "Comparison requires paired sessions - rare in practice"**
- Users don't typically run the same task with Claude and Gemini
- Natural experiment requires intentional A/B testing
- Mechanism: Feature would show "0 comparable sessions" for most users

**Objection 12: "This is an insights *dimension*, not a separate feature"**
- Insights already shows agent breakdown: `claude-code: 12, gemini-cli: 2`
- Comparison is just filtering by agent
- Mechanism: Already exists, just needs UI refinement

### Session Chaining (proposed Tier 2)

**Objection 13: "Manual linking doesn't scale - requires user annotation"**
- User must explicitly run `entire link --session <id1> --session <id2>`
- Most users won't maintain this metadata
- Mechanism: High-friction feature with low adoption

**Objection 14: "Session chains aren't insights - they're documentation"**
- Insights is quantitative (counts, durations, trends)
- Chains are qualitative (narrative, relationships)
- Mechanism: Different user need (understanding vs measuring)

### Prompt Replay (proposed Tier 3)

**Objection 15: "Replay is a code generation feature, not an insights feature"**
- Insights is retrospective (what happened?)
- Replay is prospective (do it again)
- Mechanism: Wrong command entirely

### Team Analytics (proposed Tier 3)

**Objection 16: "Team analytics is just insights with --all-users flag"**
- Same metrics (sessions, tokens, tools), different scope
- Not a new feature, just a query parameter
- Mechanism: Natural extension of insights, not separate tier

**Objection 17: "Team analytics requires privacy controls insights doesn't have"**
- Individual insights: "when am I most productive?" (private)
- Team insights: "who is least productive?" (invasive)
- Mechanism: Needs access control layer insights lacks

### Session-to-Documentation (proposed Tier 3)

**Objection 18: "Doc generation is post-session processing, not insights"**
- Insights is read-only analysis
- Doc generation is write-side transformation
- Mechanism: Different command (entire doc), not insights extension

## Phase 2: Point to Evidence Already Available

Let me examine what the existing codebase and architecture reveal:

**Evidence for "cost tracking is baseline insights":**
- UI mockup explicitly shows: `Tokens: 847K | Cost: $12.40`
- Observable fact: This is part of the spec, not an extension
- **Conclusion:** Cost tracking must be in v1, not a future enhancement

**Evidence for "search is separate from insights":**
- Existing `explain` command: per-session view (not aggregated)
- Existing `insights` (proposed): cross-session aggregation
- Observable pattern: CLI separates instance operations (explain) from aggregate operations (insights)
- **Conclusion:** Search fits the explain pattern, not insights pattern

**Evidence for "diff is per-session, not insight":**
- Diff requires: before state (checkpoint) + after state (commit)
- Insights requires: time range filter
- Observable fact: Different query patterns
- **Conclusion:** `entire diff` is a separate command, like `entire explain`

**Evidence for "multi-agent comparison is already in insights":**
- UI mockup shows: `Agents: claude-code: 12, gemini-cli: 2`
- Observable fact: Agent breakdown is a core insight
- **Missing piece:** Filter insights by agent (`entire insights --agent claude-code`)
- **Conclusion:** Not a new feature, just add filtering

**Evidence for "team analytics is natural extension":**
- Checkpoints are already pushed to `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch (shared)
- Multiple contributors → multiple session authors
- Observable fact: Data is already accessible across team
- **Missing piece:** Aggregate by author instead of filtering by time
- **Conclusion:** `entire insights --team` or `entire insights --author <name>` is low-effort extension

**Evidence for objection #9 (diff only applies to committed sessions):**
- Manual-commit strategy: sessions may never be committed
- Auto-commit strategy: every checkpoint is committed
- Observable fact: Strategy-dependent whether sessions have commits
- **Gap:** Diff is only meaningful for a subset of sessions
- **Conclusion:** Diff metric would be sparse/misleading in insights aggregation

## Phase 3: Close Escape Hatches

**Causal direction probe:**
- Does insights drive feature requests, or do feature requests define insights?
  - **Answer:** Insights is about patterns; requests are about instances
  - **Intervention:** If users ask "find sessions about X", that's search, not insights
  - **Conclusion:** User intent determines command boundary

**Counterfactual probe:**
- If session search belonged in insights, what else would we expect?
  - **Expect:** Insights would show lists of sessions, not aggregate counts
  - **Actual:** Insights UI shows totals, averages, top-K (aggregates only)
  - **Conclusion:** Search doesn't fit insights model

**Base rate probe:**
- How often do users run the same task with multiple agents?
  - **Hypothesis:** Rare (most users stick to one agent)
  - **Evidence needed:** Check actual usage - do users alternate agents?
  - **Conclusion:** Multi-agent comparison might be low-value for most users

**Selection bias probe:**
- Are we considering features because they sound impressive, or because users need them?
  - **Check:** Which features solve actual pain points?
  - **Observable:** Users can't currently find sessions (search pain) or track costs (budget pain)
  - **Conclusion:** Search and cost tracking solve real problems; session chaining is speculative

## Phase 4: Track What Collapses vs. What Stands

### Collapses Completely

❌ **"Cost/token tracking is a new feature"**
- Evidence: It's in the baseline UI mockup
- Conclusion: Must be in insights v1

❌ **"Multi-agent comparison is a separate feature"**
- Evidence: Agent breakdown already in insights UI
- Conclusion: Just add `--agent <name>` filter

❌ **"Team analytics is a separate tier"**
- Evidence: Same metrics, different scope (all users vs current user)
- Conclusion: `--team` flag extends insights naturally

### Weakened but Uncertain

⚠️ **"Search belongs in insights"**
- Evidence: Different query model (find vs aggregate)
- Uncertainty: Could insights have a "drill-down" mode?
- Conclusion: Probably separate, but might complement insights

⚠️ **"Session diff is too granular for insights"**
- Evidence: Diff is per-session, insights is cross-session
- Uncertainty: Could aggregate diff stats (avg % agent code kept)?
- Conclusion: Aggregate diff metrics might fit insights

### Still Stands

✅ **"Search is a separate command from insights"**
- Evidence: Instance query vs aggregate query
- Conclusion: `entire search` is distinct from `entire insights`

✅ **"Diff is a separate command from insights"**
- Evidence: Point-in-time operation vs time-range aggregation
- Conclusion: `entire diff` is distinct from `entire insights`

✅ **"Session chaining is documentation, not analytics"**
- Evidence: Qualitative relationships vs quantitative metrics
- Conclusion: Not an insights feature

✅ **"Prompt replay is code generation, not analytics"**
- Evidence: Prospective vs retrospective
- Conclusion: Completely separate command

✅ **"Session-to-doc is transformation, not analysis"**
- Evidence: Write vs read operation
- Conclusion: Separate command

## Phase 5: Identify Asymmetries

### Key Asymmetry Discovered: **Instance vs Aggregate**

**Instance operations** (separate commands):
- `entire explain <session-id>` - view one session
- `entire search "query"` - find sessions matching criteria
- `entire diff <session-id>` - compare agent output vs final commit
- `entire doc <session-id>` - generate doc from session

**Aggregate operations** (insights features):
- `entire insights` - patterns across sessions
- `entire insights --period week` - time-filtered aggregation
- `entire insights --repo <name>` - repo-filtered aggregation
- `entire insights --agent <name>` - agent-filtered aggregation
- `entire insights --team` - multi-user aggregation

**Design principle:** Insights is about **"what patterns emerge?"**, not **"show me session X"**

### Second Asymmetry: **Baseline vs Enhancement**

**Baseline insights (must be in v1):**
- Session counts, duration, tokens, cost (from UI mockup)
- Top repos, top tools, peak hours (from UI mockup)
- Agent breakdown (from UI mockup)
- Recent sessions list (from UI mockup)

**Natural enhancements (v2+):**
- Filter by agent: `--agent claude-code`
- Filter by repo: `--repo puddle-app`
- Team mode: `--team` or `--author <name>`
- Export formats: `--json`, `--export stats.md`
- Time comparisons: `--compare week-over-week`

**Separate commands (not insights):**
- Search, diff, doc, replay, chain

### Third Asymmetry: **Read vs Write**

**Read-only (insights territory):**
- Analyze existing sessions
- Surface patterns
- Export reports

**Write/mutate (separate commands):**
- Link sessions (creates metadata)
- Replay prompts (creates new sessions)
- Generate docs (creates files)

## Phase 6: Prevent Premature Agreement

**Self-objection 1:** "Why not put search in insights? Users might want to drill down from aggregate to instance."

**Counter:** That's what the "Recent sessions" table is for. It shows sample sessions. Full search is a different workflow with different UX (query input, ranking, pagination).

**Self-objection 2:** "Why not aggregate diff stats in insights? 'Avg % of agent code kept' seems like a useful metric."

**Counter:** That's actually compelling. If 80% of agent code is kept, it signals high trust. If 20%, it signals agent is a starting point only. This *could* be an insights metric.

**Self-objection 3:** "Team analytics seems privacy-invasive. Should it even be a feature?"

**Counter:** Good point. Needs to be opt-in and privacy-aware. But the data is already on the shared branch. The question is whether to surface it. For teams already sharing checkpoints, it's just visibility.

## Final Recommendations: Prioritized by Value/Effort

### ✅ Insights v1 (Baseline - Must Ship)

1. **Cost/token tracking** - Already in spec, must implement
   - Effort: Low (parse `usage` from transcripts)
   - Value: High (budget visibility)
   
2. **Agent breakdown with filtering** - Extend existing metric
   - Effort: Low (`--agent <name>` flag)
   - Value: Medium (helps compare agents)

3. **Export formats** - Also in spec (`--json`, `--export`)
   - Effort: Low (reuse formatters from explain)
   - Value: Medium (enables automation)

### 🎯 Insights v2 (High-Value Extensions)

4. **Team analytics** - `entire insights --team`
   - Effort: Low (aggregate across authors instead of time)
   - Value: High for teams (visibility into AI adoption)
   - **Privacy control:** Require opt-in via settings

5. **Week-over-week comparison** - `entire insights --compare`
   - Effort: Medium (run insights for 2 periods, diff the results)
   - Value: High (trend visibility: "am I using AI more or less?")

6. **Code retention metric** - `% of agent code kept in final commit`
   - Effort: Medium (requires diff between checkpoint and commit)
   - Value: High (signals agent quality/trust)
   - **Note:** Only works for committed sessions

### 🔍 Separate Commands (Not Insights)

7. **Session search** - `entire search "query"`
   - Effort: Low (ripgrep over transcript files)
   - Value: Very High (most requested feature)
   - **Why separate:** Instance query, not aggregation

8. **Session diff** - `entire diff --session <id>`
   - Effort: Medium (checkout checkpoint tree, diff with commit)
   - Value: High (shows agent vs human code)
   - **Why separate:** Per-session operation

9. **Session-aware code review** - `entire annotate <commit>`
   - Effort: Medium (extract checkpoint ID from trailer, format for PR)
   - Value: Very High for teams (PR context)
   - **Why separate:** PR workflow, not analytics

### ❌ Defer/Reconsider

10. **Session chaining** - `entire link --session <id1> <id2>`
    - Effort: Medium (metadata storage + UI)
    - Value: Low (manual process, low adoption)
    - **Reasoning:** Nice-to-have, not essential

11. **Prompt replay** - `entire replay --session <id>`
    - Effort: High (LLM integration, prompt extraction, context mapping)
    - Value: High but speculative (unproven user need)
    - **Reasoning:** Wait for validated demand

12. **Session-to-doc** - `entire doc --session <id>`
    - Effort: High (LLM integration, template design)
    - Value: Medium (already have explain for summaries)
    - **Reasoning:** Incremental improvement over explain

## Compounding Value Matrix

Features that create multiplicative value when combined:

```
insights --team + --compare
  → "Is our team using AI more this month than last?"
  
insights --agent claude-code + --repo puddle-app
  → "How much Claude Code usage on our main repo?"
  
search "authentication" → explain <session-id> → diff <session-id>
  → Workflow: Find → Understand → Evaluate
  
insights + annotate
  → Insights shows "top productive sessions" → annotate shows what code they produced
```

**Highest compounding value:** search + explain + diff (investigation workflow)

## Implementation Priority (Recommended)

**Sprint 1: Insights v1 + Search**
1. Cost/token tracking (baseline insights)
2. Agent filtering (extend insights)
3. Export formats (baseline insights)
4. Session search (separate command) ← highest user value

**Sprint 2: Code Quality Metrics**
5. Code retention metric (insights v2)
6. Session diff (separate command)

**Sprint 3: Team Features**
7. Team analytics (insights v2)
8. Session-aware code review (separate command)

**Sprint 4+: Advanced**
9. Week-over-week comparison (insights v2)
10. Other features based on user feedback

---

## The Robust Conclusion

**Insights should focus on aggregation and patterns. Instance operations (search, diff, doc) belong in separate commands.**

This survives rigorous examination because:
1. **Evidence from UI mockup:** Insights is aggregate metrics (totals, averages, top-K)
2. **Evidence from user workflows:** Different intents (measure vs find vs transform)
3. **Evidence from architecture:** CLI already separates instance (explain) from future aggregate (insights)
4. **Asymmetry identified:** Read/aggregate (insights) vs read/instance (search) vs write (link, doc)

**The three most valuable features to build:**
1. **Session search** - solves "I can't find that session where..." pain
2. **Cost/token tracking** - solves "how much am I spending?" pain  
3. **Session diff** - solves "did the agent write good code?" pain

**These three are separate concerns but form a coherent "session intelligence" layer.**

   251→func runExplainCheckpoint(w, errW io.Writer, checkpointIDPrefix string, noPager, verbose, full, rawTranscript, generate, force, searchAll bool, export, showcase bool, format, outputFile string) error {

   357→// generateCheckpointSummary generates an AI summary for a checkpoint and persists it.
   358→// The summary is generated from the scoped transcript (only this checkpoint's portion),

   360→func generateCheckpointSummary(w, _ io.Writer, store *checkpoint.GitStore, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, cpSummary *checkpoint.CheckpointSummary, content *checkpoint.SessionContent, force bool) error {
   361→	// Check if summary already exists
   362→	if content.Metadata.Summary != nil && !force {
   363→		return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s already has a summary (use --force to regenerate)", checkpointID)
   364→	}
   365→
   366→	// Check if transcript exists
   367→	if len(content.Transcript) == 0 {
   368→		return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s has no transcript to summarize", checkpointID)
   369→	}
   370→
   371→	// Scope the transcript to only this checkpoint's portion
   372→	scopedTranscript := scopeTranscriptForCheckpoint(content.Transcript, content.Metadata.GetTranscriptStart())
   373→	if len(scopedTranscript) == 0 {
   374→		return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s has no transcript content for this checkpoint (scoped)", checkpointID)
   375→	}
   376→
   377→	// Generate summary using shared helper
   378→	ctx := context.Background()
   379→	logging.Info(ctx, "generating checkpoint summary")
   380→
   381→	summary, err := summarize.GenerateFromTranscript(ctx, scopedTranscript, cpSummary.FilesTouched, nil)
   382→	if err != nil {
   383→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate summary: %w", err)
   384→	}
   385→
   386→	// Persist the summary
   387→	if err := store.UpdateSummary(ctx, checkpointID, summary); err != nil {
   388→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save summary: %w", err)
   389→	}
   390→
   391→	fmt.Fprintln(w, "✓ Summary generated and saved")
   392→	return nil
   393→}
